title: Methods
text:
This project is a work in progress and the results should be read as preliminary.
This project analyses co-occurrence patterns of plant taxa across space, time, and biological resolution using fossil pollen records, modern vegetation records, co-located climate data, site coordinates, and plant functional traits. The central aim is to quantify how much of the observed co-occurrence signal is explained by shared abiotic responses, spatial or spatiotemporal structure, and residual species-species association signals.
The project is part of the BIODYNAMICS initiative.




All primary vegetation, climate, coordinate, and trait inputs are sourced from VegVault, a harmonised SQLite database that combines fossil pollen archives, modern vegetation datasets, co-registered climate reconstructions, and plant functional traits. Using a single harmonised data source keeps site identifiers, sample ages, coordinates, taxonomy, and climate values consistent across the paleo, modern, and trait workflows. For each analysis, records are extracted for the spatial window, temporal range, data source, and predictor set defined by the active configuration in config.yml.






NoteTechnical details - data extraction





The function extract_data_from_vegvault() queries a local VegVault SQLite database and returns a unified tidy object containing community and abiotic records for the requested analysis. Coordinates are extracted with extract_dataset_coordinates(), which records one coordinate pair per dataset rather than one coordinate pair per sample. Database presence and accessibility are checked at session startup with validate_vegvault_presence().
Configuration-controlled extraction filters:

Spatial window: x_lim and y_lim
Temporal window: age_lim
Dataset types: sel_dataset_type
Abiotic variables: sel_abiotic_var_name
Target store root: target_store

Current data families:

Climate predictors represent the shared abiotic response component of the joint species distribution models. Paleo analyses use CHELSA-TraCE21k bioclimatic variables co-registered with the pollen records in VegVault. The broad candidate set includes variables describing mean thermal energy, temperature seasonality and extremes, annual precipitation, and seasonal precipitation.
To prevent redundant predictors from inflating coefficient uncertainty, the pipeline screens candidate climate variables before model fitting. The current workflow removes invariant predictors, evaluates collinearity, and retains a non-redundant predictor subset for the active dataset.






NoteTechnical details - abiotic processing

Predictor screening and scaling are performed inside each target store, so each spatial unit, time-slice workflow, and data source can have its own model-ready predictor matrix.






Plant traits are used to build functional-type classifications that can be compared with genus- and family-level community matrices. The traits workflow extracts raw trait values from VegVault, flags problematic values, applies curated corrections, aggregates validated trait values to taxa, and clusters taxa into functional types. Functional types are generated as reference classifications and then consumed by the spatial-resolution pipelines.






NoteTechnical details - trait processing

Key helper functions include load_trait_records_from_vegvault(), filter_complete_trait_records(), correct_trait_records(), aggregate_trait_values(), and assign_functional_type_clusters().







The current project structure is broader than the original two-pipeline design. The analysis now spans paleo and modern data sources, three spatial scales, temporal slices through the late Quaternary, and multiple taxonomic or functional resolutions.






ImportantComplementary analysis axes





pipeline_paleo_temporal.R fits the shared modelling core independently across paleo time slices. Each branch receives a target age from tarchetypes::tar_map(), filters the aligned sample set to that time slice, fits a model, calculates variance decomposition, and summarises temporal trajectories.
Configurations: project_paleo_temporal_europe, project_paleo_temporal_america, project_paleo_temporal_asia



pipeline_paleo_spatial_resolution.R and pipeline_modern_spatial_resolution.R run the shared modelling core independently for geographic units defined in Data/Input/spatial_grid.csv. Spatial units are stored separately with store_suffix, so each unit has its own target store and progress graph.
Configurations: project_paleo_spatial_continental, project_paleo_spatial_regional, project_paleo_spatial_local, project_modern_spatial_continental, project_modern_spatial_regional, project_modern_spatial_local



Spatial-resolution pipelines branch over community resolution. Paleo spatial analyses compare genus, family, and functional-type matrices. Modern spatial analyses support genus, family, and functional-type variants routed through the current branch labels.
Resolution branches: genus, family, and functional type.



The analytical core is shared across these axes. The main differences are how samples are selected, which community resolution is supplied to the model, and whether the spatial component is purely spatial or spatiotemporal.

Vegetation records, climate data, and coordinates are queried from a local VegVault SQLite database for the active configuration. The extraction produces parallel data objects that remain separate through preprocessing and are only merged at sample alignment and model assembly.






NoteTechnical details

Target
Function

The extraction segment is reused by paleo, modern, and development pipelines. Target store isolation is controlled by the active configuration and, for spatial workflows, by store_suffix.






Community data are extracted from the VegVault result object and converted into the long-format structure expected by downstream preprocessing. This stage keeps the raw taxon names and sample metadata available for classification, interpolation, filtering, and audit checks.






NoteTechnical details

Step
Target or helper
Role

Taxonomic classification resolves source taxon names to a consistent project taxonomy. The workflow combines automated classification, project-specific auxiliary tables, and missing-taxon reporting so unresolved or manually corrected cases remain explicit.






NoteTechnical details

This stage supports the later genus, family, and functional-type branches.






Paleo community preparation transforms fossil pollen counts into a filtered, classified, and temporally standardised community table. The workflow converts counts to proportions, propagates sample ages, extracts age uncertainty, interpolates irregular records to the configured temporal grid, removes non-plant taxa, resolves taxonomic resolution, and applies data-density filters.






NoteTechnical details

Age uncertainty and interpolation are central to the paleo workflow because fossil samples are irregularly spaced and have uncertainty from age-depth modelling.






Modern community preparation shares the same broad goal as the paleo workflow but has different quality-control problems. Modern vegetation data are checked for impossible values, exact duplicates, colocated records, and source-specific aggregation cases before they are filtered and supplied to the shared modelling stack.

Cross-database colocations are tracked rather than silently merged unless the aggregation rules explicitly allow it. This keeps modern data processing auditable.






After shared community preparation, spatial-resolution pipelines branch over biological resolution. The same input data can be routed to genus-level, family-level, or functional-type community matrices before alignment and model fitting.






NoteTechnical details

Modern segment: pipe_segment_community_by_resolution_modern.R

Resolve taxa to family-level community columns


Functional type

Key helpers include classify_taxonomic_resolution(), resolve_classification_to_finest_rank(), classify_to_functional_type(), and replace_missing_community_counts_with_zeros().
Functional-type classifications are generated before the resolution branches need them. Spatial-resolution pipelines read those classifications with helpers such as resolve_functional_type_classification_path_from_store() and load_functional_type_classification().






Data alignment defines which samples enter the model. The pipeline retains only sample identifiers that can be matched across community data, abiotic predictors, and coordinates.






NoteTechnical details





Spatial segment: pipe_segment_sample_alignment.R
Temporal segment: pipe_segment_sample_filter_age.R



Path
Sample-selection logic




Spatial
align_sample_ids() computes the intersection across community, abiotic, and coordinate records for the whole spatial unit


Temporal
The time-slice branch supplies an age value and filters aligned samples to that target slice


Validation
validate_sample_count() checks whether enough samples remain



All model matrices use a consistent sample-key convention derived from dataset_name and age. This allows community, abiotic, coordinate, and spatial predictor matrices to be checked for identical row order before fitting.






The aligned data are converted into matrix form before fitting. Community data are made wide and binarised, abiotic predictors are prepared and scaled, coordinates are projected, and spatial predictors are calculated.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segments: pipe_segment_model_input.R, pipe_segment_model_prepare_response.R, pipe_segment_model_spatial_shared.R, pipe_segment_model_spatial_samples.R, and pipe_segment_model_assemble.R



Target or function
Description




prepare_community_for_fit()
Converts long community records to a model matrix


compute_community_presence_absence()
Computes the binary presence/absence response


prepare_abiotic_for_fit()
Prepares abiotic predictors in wide form


scale_abiotic_for_fit()
Scales abiotic predictors and saves scaling attributes


prepare_coords_for_fit()
Prepares coordinate tables for modelling


project_coords_to_metric()
Projects coordinates to a metric coordinate reference system


compute_spatial_mev()
Computes spatial Moran Eigenvector Maps


compute_spatiotemporal_mev()
Computes spatiotemporal Moran Eigenvector Maps


prepare_spatial_predictors_for_fit()
Expands or aligns MEM predictors to model samples


scale_spatial_for_fit()
Scales MEM predictors


build_jsdm_fit_input()
Validates and assembles the final model input list



For spatial analyses, MEMs are computed from geographic distances among sites. For temporal analyses, MEMs can be computed from sample-level spatiotemporal coordinates so that broad temporal and spatial autocorrelation are handled together.






The model is a Joint Species Distribution Model fitted with {sjSDM}. This framework fits all taxa jointly and estimates residual covariance among taxa after accounting for shared climate and spatial structure. The residual covariance is the association signal of interest, but it is interpreted cautiously because unmeasured environment, dispersal, history, and true interactions can all contribute to it.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_model_fit.R



Target or function
Description




build_jsdm_environment_formula()
Builds the environmental model formula


fit_jsdm_model()
Fits the {sjSDM} model


compute_jsdm_se()
Computes post-hoc standard errors


evaluate_jsdm()
Summarises model fit and species-level performance


diagnose_jsdm_convergence()
Diagnoses model convergence


diagnose_sjsdm_gpu_runtime()
Reports GPU runtime availability without aborting


validate_sjsdm_gpu_runtime()
Enforces GPU requirements before fitting



Model components:

Environment: non-redundant climate predictors and, where configured, interactions with age.
Space: MEM predictors used as a spatial or spatiotemporal structure component.
Association: residual low-rank covariance structure estimated by {sjSDM}.
Response: binary presence/absence community matrix.

The project previously used HMSC-style MCMC modelling. The workflow was migrated to {sjSDM} because gradient-descent fitting with optional GPU support is more practical for the large community matrices used here.






After fitting, the model is decomposed into abiotic, spatial, and association components. This is the main comparative quantity used across spatial scale, time, data source, and biological resolution.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_model_anova.R



Target or function
Description




compute_jsdm_variance_partition()
Runs Monte Carlo ANOVA decomposition for the fitted model


extract_jsdm_variance_fractions()
Extracts named A, S, B, and shared fractions


aggregate_jsdm_variance_components()
Aggregates decomposition outputs across temporal branches


compute_shapley_variance_components()
Converts raw fractions into comparable component summaries



Components:

A: variance associated with abiotic predictors.
S: variance associated with spatial or spatiotemporal MEM predictors.
B: residual association signal from the joint model covariance structure.
Shared fractions: variance jointly attributable to combinations of A, S, and B.

Shared fractions are handled explicitly because climate, space, and association structure are not independent in ecological data.






Temporal analyses also calculate network metrics directly from the binarised community matrix. These metrics provide a model-independent description of co-occurrence structure through time.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segments: pipe_segment_network_metrics.R and pipe_segment_network_summary_by_age.R



Target or function
Description




compute_network_metrics()
Calculates network-level metrics from a binary community matrix


plot_network_metrics_by_age()
Visualises temporal network trajectories



Metrics:

Connectance: proportion of realised links in the network.
Nestedness: degree to which specialist taxa occur within subsets of broader assemblages.
Modularity: degree to which the network is divided into sub-communities.







The fitted model stack is also used for prediction and exploratory visualisation. These outputs are useful for checking model behaviour and communicating palaeoecological dynamics, but they remain preliminary while the analysis is being developed.






NoteTechnical details





Project-wide prediction helpers include build_land_prediction_grid() and predict_spatial_resolution_grid_age(). Presentation-specific frame and animation helpers are maintained beside the IAVS 2026 presentation rather than in the global function API.
Summary and plotting helpers include summarise_spatial_variance_stack(), summarise_spatial_biotic_component(), plot_spatial_variance_stack(), plot_spatial_biotic_component(), and plot_anova_components_by_age().







The active pipeline scripts live in R/Pipelines/. Reusable pipe segments live in R/Pipelines/_pipes/. The store path is built from the active configuration’s target_store, an optional spatial store_suffix, and the pipeline script name.







Pipeline
Purpose

Compact paleo development workflow


pipeline_paleo_temporal.R
Paleo temporal models across time slices


pipeline_paleo_spatial_resolution.R

pipeline_paleo_resolution_test.R
Development check for paleo resolution routing


pipeline_modern_spatial_resolution.R
Modern spatial models across geographic units and biological resolutions


pipeline_modern_spatial_resolution_test.R
Development check for modern spatial-resolution routing


pipeline_traits_reference.R
Trait extraction, quality control, and functional-type reference generation






The current configuration names are defined in config.yml. They replace older names that were used before the paleo, modern, and traits workflows were separated.







Configuration
Role

project_cz_modern
Small modern development workflow

Trait processing and functional-type reference workflow

Paleo temporal North America


project_paleo_temporal_asia
Paleo temporal northern Asia


project_paleo_spatial_continental
Paleo spatial continental scale

Paleo spatial regional scale

Paleo spatial local scale

project_modern_spatial_local

The live graphs below are generated by targets::tar_visnetwork() through the project progress helpers. They show build state and dependencies rather than final scientific results.























The website intentionally exposes the method, code structure, progress graphs, function reference, and conference material while keeping the result interpretation provisional. The model outputs, spatial comparisons, temporal trajectories, prediction experiments, and functional-type summaries are still being checked and should not be treated as final manuscript results.

title: Methods
text:
Vegetation records, climate data, and coordinates are queried from a local VegVault SQLite database for the active configuration. The extraction produces parallel data objects that remain separate through preprocessing and are only merged at sample alignment and model assembly.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_vegvault_extract.R



Target
Function
Description




data_vegvault_extracted
extract_data_from_vegvault()
Raw community and abiotic records from VegVault


data_coords
extract_dataset_coordinates()
One coordinate pair per dataset_name


validation_available_core_count
validate_available_core_count()
Guard for the minimum number of pollen cores



The extraction segment is reused by paleo, modern, and development pipelines. Target store isolation is controlled by the active configuration and, for spatial workflows, by store_suffix.






Community data are extracted from the VegVault result object and converted into the long-format structure expected by downstream preprocessing. This stage keeps the raw taxon names and sample metadata available for classification, interpolation, filtering, and audit checks.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_community_extract.R



Step
Target or helper
Role




Community extraction
extract_community_records()
Extract nested community records from the VegVault object


Long conversion
reshape_community_to_long()
Reshape community records to tidy long format


Age join
join_sample_ages()
Join sample ages before interpolation or filtering


Pollen sums
summarise_pollen_counts_by_sample()
Summarise pollen sums used in proportional filtering









Taxonomic classification resolves source taxon names to a consistent project taxonomy. The workflow combines automated classification, project-specific auxiliary tables, and missing-taxon reporting so unresolved or manually corrected cases remain explicit.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_taxa_classification.R



Target or helper
Description




load_taxa_classification()
Loads taxonomic classifications


load_auxiliary_classification_table()
Loads project-specific manual classifications


build_combined_classification_table()
Builds the combined automatic and auxiliary classification table


select_unclassified_taxa()
Selects unresolved taxa


save_missing_taxa_template()
Saves missing-taxon templates for review


validate_taxa_classification_coverage()
Validates taxonomic-classification coverage



This stage supports the later genus, family, and functional-type branches.






Paleo community preparation transforms fossil pollen counts into a filtered, classified, and temporally standardised community table. The workflow converts counts to proportions, propagates sample ages, extracts age uncertainty, interpolates irregular records to the configured temporal grid, removes non-plant taxa, resolves taxonomic resolution, and applies data-density filters.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_community_prepare_paleo.R



Step
Target or function
Description




Proportions
prepare_community_proportions()
Prepare counts as proportional abundance


Age uncertainty
extract_age_uncertainty_from_vegvault()
Retrieves age uncertainty information


Shared inputs
build_shared_interpolation_data()
Builds read-only shared-memory inputs for interpolation workers


Interpolation index
build_community_interpolation_index()
Builds small per-dataset branch metadata


Dataset interpolation
interpolate_community_dataset_from_shared_inputs()
Interpolates one dataset from shared inputs


Paleo community interpolation
interpolate_paleo_community_with_age_uncertainty()
Interpolates consensus ages and fossil age-model iterations


Plantae filter
filter_community_to_plantae()
Retains plant records


Proportion filter
filter_community_by_minimum_proportion()
Removes low-proportion records


Core and sample filters
filter_community_by_minimum_core_count(), filter_community_by_minimum_sample_count()
Enforce data-density requirements


Taxon ranking
select_top_taxa_by_group_occurrence()
Retains the most widespread taxa


Matrix guard
validate_community_taxon_count()
Stops model fitting when too few taxa remain



Age uncertainty and interpolation are central to the paleo workflow because fossil samples are irregularly spaced and have uncertainty from age-depth modelling.






Modern community preparation shares the same broad goal as the paleo workflow but has different quality-control problems. Modern vegetation data are checked for impossible values, exact duplicates, colocated records, and source-specific aggregation cases before they are filtered and supplied to the shared modelling stack.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_community_prepare_modern.R



Step
Target or function
Description




Quality report
evaluate_modern_data_quality()
Evaluates modern-data quality checks


Impossible values

Diagnoses invalid ages, coordinates, or abundance values


Duplicate sites

Diagnoses repeated site metadata


Duplicate communities

Colocated records

Diagnoses records sharing coordinates and age


Deduplication

Removes exact duplicates deterministically


Colocated aggregation

Aggregates eligible colocated records


Source validation
validate_community_source()
Checks community source labels



Cross-database colocations are tracked rather than silently merged unless the aggregation rules explicitly allow it. This keeps modern data processing auditable.






After shared community preparation, spatial-resolution pipelines branch over biological resolution. The same input data can be routed to genus-level, family-level, or functional-type community matrices before alignment and model fitting.






NoteTechnical details





Paleo segment: pipe_segment_community_by_resolution_paleo.R
Modern segment: pipe_segment_community_by_resolution_modern.R



Resolution
Main operation




Genus
Resolve taxa to genus-level community columns


Family
Resolve taxa to family-level community columns


Functional type
Collapse taxon presences to functional-type groups



Key helpers include classify_taxonomic_resolution(), resolve_classification_to_finest_rank(), classify_to_functional_type(), and replace_missing_community_counts_with_zeros().
Functional-type classifications are generated before the resolution branches need them. Spatial-resolution pipelines read those classifications with helpers such as resolve_functional_type_classification_path_from_store() and load_functional_type_classification().






Data alignment defines which samples enter the model. The pipeline retains only sample identifiers that can be matched across community data, abiotic predictors, and coordinates.






NoteTechnical details





Spatial segment: pipe_segment_sample_alignment.R
Temporal segment: pipe_segment_sample_filter_age.R



Path
Sample-selection logic




Spatial
align_sample_ids() computes the intersection across community, abiotic, and coordinate records for the whole spatial unit


Temporal
The time-slice branch supplies an age value and filters aligned samples to that target slice


Validation
validate_sample_count() checks whether enough samples remain



All model matrices use a consistent sample-key convention derived from dataset_name and age. This allows community, abiotic, coordinate, and spatial predictor matrices to be checked for identical row order before fitting.






The aligned data are converted into matrix form before fitting. Community data are made wide and binarised, abiotic predictors are prepared and scaled, coordinates are projected, and spatial predictors are calculated.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segments: pipe_segment_model_input.R, pipe_segment_model_prepare_response.R, pipe_segment_model_spatial_shared.R, pipe_segment_model_spatial_samples.R, and pipe_segment_model_assemble.R



Target or function
Description




prepare_community_for_fit()
Converts long community records to a model matrix


compute_community_presence_absence()
Computes the binary presence/absence response


prepare_abiotic_for_fit()
Prepares abiotic predictors in wide form


scale_abiotic_for_fit()
Scales abiotic predictors and saves scaling attributes


prepare_coords_for_fit()
Prepares coordinate tables for modelling


project_coords_to_metric()
Projects coordinates to a metric coordinate reference system


compute_spatial_mev()
Computes spatial Moran Eigenvector Maps


compute_spatiotemporal_mev()
Computes spatiotemporal Moran Eigenvector Maps


prepare_spatial_predictors_for_fit()
Expands or aligns MEM predictors to model samples


scale_spatial_for_fit()
Scales MEM predictors


build_jsdm_fit_input()
Validates and assembles the final model input list



For spatial analyses, MEMs are computed from geographic distances among sites. For temporal analyses, MEMs can be computed from sample-level spatiotemporal coordinates so that broad temporal and spatial autocorrelation are handled together.






The model is a Joint Species Distribution Model fitted with {sjSDM}. This framework fits all taxa jointly and estimates residual covariance among taxa after accounting for shared climate and spatial structure. The residual covariance is the association signal of interest, but it is interpreted cautiously because unmeasured environment, dispersal, history, and true interactions can all contribute to it.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_model_fit.R



Target or function
Description




build_jsdm_environment_formula()
Builds the environmental model formula


fit_jsdm_model()
Fits the {sjSDM} model


compute_jsdm_se()
Computes post-hoc standard errors


evaluate_jsdm()
Summarises model fit and species-level performance


diagnose_jsdm_convergence()
Diagnoses model convergence


diagnose_sjsdm_gpu_runtime()
Reports GPU runtime availability without aborting


validate_sjsdm_gpu_runtime()
Enforces GPU requirements before fitting



Model components:

Environment: non-redundant climate predictors and, where configured, interactions with age.
Space: MEM predictors used as a spatial or spatiotemporal structure component.
Association: residual low-rank covariance structure estimated by {sjSDM}.
Response: binary presence/absence community matrix.

The project previously used HMSC-style MCMC modelling. The workflow was migrated to {sjSDM} because gradient-descent fitting with optional GPU support is more practical for the large community matrices used here.






After fitting, the model is decomposed into abiotic, spatial, and association components. This is the main comparative quantity used across spatial scale, time, data source, and biological resolution.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segment: pipe_segment_model_anova.R



Target or function
Description




compute_jsdm_variance_partition()
Runs Monte Carlo ANOVA decomposition for the fitted model


extract_jsdm_variance_fractions()
Extracts named A, S, B, and shared fractions


aggregate_jsdm_variance_components()
Aggregates decomposition outputs across temporal branches


compute_shapley_variance_components()
Converts raw fractions into comparable component summaries



Components:

A: variance associated with abiotic predictors.
S: variance associated with spatial or spatiotemporal MEM predictors.
B: residual association signal from the joint model covariance structure.
Shared fractions: variance jointly attributable to combinations of A, S, and B.

Shared fractions are handled explicitly because climate, space, and association structure are not independent in ecological data.






Temporal analyses also calculate network metrics directly from the binarised community matrix. These metrics provide a model-independent description of co-occurrence structure through time.






NoteTechnical details





Pipe segments: pipe_segment_network_metrics.R and pipe_segment_network_summary_by_age.R



Target or function
Description




compute_network_metrics()
Calculates network-level metrics from a binary community matrix


plot_network_metrics_by_age()
Visualises temporal network trajectories



Metrics:

Connectance: proportion of realised links in the network.
Nestedness: degree to which specialist taxa occur within subsets of broader assemblages.
Modularity: degree to which the network is divided into sub-communities.







The fitted model stack is also used for prediction and exploratory visualisation. These outputs are useful for checking model behaviour and communicating palaeoecological dynamics, but they remain preliminary while the analysis is being developed.






NoteTechnical details





Project-wide prediction helpers include build_land_prediction_grid() and predict_spatial_resolution_grid_age(). Presentation-specific frame and animation helpers are maintained beside the IAVS 2026 presentation rather than in the global function API.
Summary and plotting helpers include summarise_spatial_variance_stack(), summarise_spatial_biotic_component(), plot_spatial_variance_stack(), plot_spatial_biotic_component(), and plot_anova_components_by_age().

title: validate_taxa_classification_coverage()
text:
validate_taxa_classification_coverage


R Documentation




Validate taxonomic-classification coverage


Description


Validates that all community taxa have been classified. When missing taxa are found, stops with an informative error message listing the count of unclassified taxa. Returns ‘TRUE’ invisibly when no taxa are missing.


Usage

validate_taxa_classification_coverage(
  vec_taxa_without_classification,
  file_missing_taxa_template = NULL
)


Arguments




vec_taxa_without_classification



A character vector of taxon names that could not be classified automatically or via the auxiliary table. An empty vector (‘character(0)’) signals full coverage and causes the function to return silently.





file_missing_taxa_template



‘NULL’ by default. Optional placeholder for a targets file dependency. When supplied in a pipeline, it ensures the missing taxa CSV is written before the error is raised.





Details


The missing taxa are stored as a targets object ‘data_missing_taxa_template’ in the pipeline store. Inspect them with ‘targets::tar_read("data_missing_taxa_template")’. During a pipeline run the same rows are also appended to ‘Data/Input/missing_taxa_template.csv’ for manual review. The object is a ‘tibble’ with columns ‘sel_name’, ‘kingdom’, ‘phylum’, ‘class’, ‘order’, ‘family’, ‘genus’, and ‘species’; rank columns are left as ‘NA’ for manual completion. Fill in the missing classifications and copy or append rows to ‘Data/Input/aux_classification_table.csv’, then re-run the pipeline. Use the helper script in ‘R/03_Supplementary_analyses/Classification/’ to coalesce templates across all pipeline stores into one CSV.


Value


‘TRUE’ invisibly when every taxon is classified. Stops with an error when any taxa are missing.


See Also


[load_auxiliary_classification_table()], [build_combined_classification_table()], [select_unclassified_taxa()]


Examples

validate_taxa_classification_coverage(
  vec_taxa_without_classification = base::character(0)
)

base::try(
  validate_taxa_classification_coverage(
    vec_taxa_without_classification = base::c("Taxon_a")
  )
)

title: validate_sample_count()
text:
validate_sample_count


R Documentation




Validate Sample Count


Description


Guards against running downstream data preparation and model fitting on a time slice with too few ‘(dataset_name, age)’ combinations. Returns ‘data_sample_ids’ unchanged when the row count is at least ‘minimum_sample_count’. Stops with an informative error when the count falls below the threshold, preventing expensive model fitting on near-empty slices.


Usage

validate_sample_count(data_sample_ids = NULL, minimum_sample_count = 1)


Arguments




data_sample_ids



A data frame with at least the columns ‘dataset_name’ and ‘age’, as returned by ‘align_sample_ids()’. Each row represents one valid ‘(dataset_name, age)’ pair.





minimum_sample_count



A single positive integer giving the minimum number of samples (rows) required to proceed with data preparation and model fitting. Default is 1.





Details


The check counts ‘nrow(data_sample_ids)’ after the time-slice filter has been applied by ‘align_sample_ids(subset_age = …)’. If the count falls below ‘minimum_sample_count’, ‘cli::cli_abort()’ is called with a message that reports the actual sample count and the threshold, allowing the user to adjust the configuration or the input data. This check is intended to be placed in the per-slice pipeline (e.g. ‘pipe_segment_sample_filter_age’) so that slices without sufficient data fail immediately, before any expensive preparation or model fitting.


Value


The input ‘data_sample_ids’ unchanged, when ‘nrow(data_sample_ids) >= minimum_sample_count’.


See Also


[align_sample_ids()], [validate_community_taxon_count()]

title: summarise_taxonomic_group_traits()
text:
summarise_taxonomic_group_traits


R Documentation




Summarise Traits Within a Taxonomic Group


Description


Resolves the taxonomic group containing ‘focal_taxon’, collects records for taxa in that group and ‘trait_domain’, and returns per-taxon summary statistics sorted by ‘median’.


Usage

summarise_taxonomic_group_traits(
  data_trait_records,
  data_taxon_classification,
  focal_taxon,
  trait_domain,
  taxonomic_rank = "family",
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_trait_records



A data frame of raw trait observations. Must contain columns ‘taxon_name’ (character), ‘trait_domain_name’ (character), and ‘trait_value’ (numeric).





data_taxon_classification



A data frame mapping taxon names to taxonomic ranks. Must contain ‘sel_name’ and the column named by ‘taxonomic_rank’.





focal_taxon



Character scalar. Name of the focal taxon to look up.





trait_domain



Character scalar. Trait domain to summarise (matched against ‘trait_domain_name’ in ‘data_trait_records’).





taxonomic_rank



Character scalar. Name of the taxonomic rank column in ‘data_taxon_classification’ to use for grouping (e.g. ‘"family"’, ‘"genus"’, ‘"order"’). Defaults to ‘"family"’.





verbose



Logical. If ‘TRUE’ (default), progress messages are printed to the console via ‘cli’.





Details



The function looks up ‘focal_taxon’ in ‘data_taxon_classification’ to resolve ‘taxonomic_rank’.
All taxa sharing that rank value are identified.
‘data_trait_records’ is filtered to those taxa and ‘trait_domain’, then grouped by ‘taxon_name’.
If the rank value cannot be resolved (taxon absent from classification or the rank column is ‘NA’), only the focal taxon’s own records are summarised.



Value


A tibble with one row per taxon that has data for ‘trait_domain’ within the same ‘taxonomic_rank’ group as ‘focal_taxon’. Columns: ‘taxon_name’, ‘n_records’, ‘minimum’, ‘lower_quartile’, ‘median’, ‘mean’, ‘upper_quartile’, and ‘maximum’. Rows are sorted ascending by ‘median’. If the focal taxon or rank value cannot be resolved, only records for ‘focal_taxon’ are summarised.


See Also


[write_trait_quality_control_report()], [plot_focal_trait_distribution()]


Examples

## Not run:
data_aux_classification <-
  readr::read_csv(
    here::here("Data/Input/aux_classification_table.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

data_taxonomic_trait_summary <-
  summarise_taxonomic_group_traits(
    data_trait_records = data_traits_raw,
    data_taxon_classification = data_aux_classification,
    focal_taxon = "Anacyclus clavatus",
    trait_domain = "Leaf Area"
  )

## End(Not run)

Scale Spatial Predictors for Model Fitting


Description


Centres and scales all spatial predictor columns, records the scaling attributes for later back-transformation, and returns both the scaled data frame and the attributes as a named list.


Usage

scale_spatial_for_fit(data_spatial = NULL)


Arguments




data_spatial



A data frame with row names in the format ’"<dataset_name>__<age>"’ and numeric columns containing spatial predictor variables (e.g. ‘coord_x_km’, ‘coord_y_km’), as returned by ‘prepare_spatial_predictors_for_fit()’.

Value

title: save_continental_functional_type_classification()
text:
save_continental_functional_type_classification


R Documentation




Save Functional-Type Classification for One Continental Unit


Description


Saves a pre-computed functional-type classification tibble as a dated ‘.qs’ file in ‘path_processed’. The classification is produced upstream by ‘assign_functional_type_clusters()’ via the ‘data_functional_type_classification_continent’ pipeline target.


Usage

save_continental_functional_type_classification(
  continent_id,
  data_functional_type_classification,
  path_classification_directory = here::here("Data/Processed/Traits"),
  classification_source_prefix = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




continent_id



A single non-empty character string identifying the continental unit (e.g. ‘"europe"’, ‘"america"’, ‘"asia"’). Used only for naming the output file.





data_functional_type_classification



A data frame containing the functional-type classification, as returned in the ‘classification’ element of ‘assign_functional_type_clusters()’. Typically has columns ‘taxon_name’, ‘functional_type’, and ‘silhouette_width’.





path_classification_directory



A single character string giving the directory where the ‘.qs’ output file will be written. Default: ‘here::here("Data/Processed/Traits")’.





classification_source_prefix



Optional single non-empty character string to prepend to the ‘continent_id’ portion of the file name. Use ‘NULL’ (default) for the historical paleo/global naming convention, or ‘"modern"’ for modern-data functional-type classifications.





verbose



Logical. If ‘TRUE’ (default), progress messages are printed to the console via ‘cli’.





Details


Steps performed:




Validate arguments.




Save ‘data_functional_type_classification’ with ‘RUtilpol::save_latest_file()’ as a dated ‘.qs’ file in ‘path_classification_directory’. The file is only overwritten when the content has changed since the previous version.




Resolve the path of the just-saved file via ‘RUtilpol::get_latest_file_name()’.




Return the file path as a character string.




Data filtering, distance computation, hierarchical clustering, ft-groups selection are all handled upstream by ‘select_continental_trait_table()’, ‘compute_trait_dissimilarity()’, ‘fit_hierarchical_clustering()’, and ‘assign_functional_type_clusters()’ respectively.


Value


A single character string: the absolute path to the ‘.qs’ file that was written. The file is saved via ‘RUtilpol::save_latest_file()’ using the name stem ‘data_functional_type_classification_continent_id’ when ‘classification_source_prefix = NULL’, or ‘data_functional_type_classification_classification_source_prefix_continent_id’ otherwise. The final file name includes a date stamp and content hash appended by ‘RUtilpol’ (e.g. ’data_functional_type_classification_europe_2026-05-07__abc123__.qs’).


See Also


[select_continental_trait_table()], [compute_trait_dissimilarity()], [fit_hierarchical_clustering()], [assign_functional_type_clusters()]

Get Scale ID from Current Targets Store Path


Description


Determines whether the currently active targets store corresponds to a spatial unit by inspecting the store path and checking it against the project’s spatial grid CSV catalogue. Returns the ‘scale_id’ string for spatial pipelines, or ‘NULL’ for non-spatial (named-project) pipelines.

Details


The store path convention for spatial pipelines is: ‘target_store/scale_id/pipeline_name/’. For non-spatial pipelines (e.g. ‘Data/targets/cz_paleo/pipeline_paleo_core/’) the candidate (‘"project_cz_paleo"’) is not in the CSV, so ‘NULL’ is returned. R Documentation




Assess Cross-Validation Feasibility


Description


Evaluates full-model and candidate training-partition diagnostics and selects the first viable cross-validation strategy.


Usage

resolve_cross_validation_strategy(
  data_partition_diagnostics = NULL,
  min_train_locations = NULL,
  min_train_samples = NULL,
  min_train_taxa = NULL,
  min_mem_locations = NULL
)


Arguments




data_partition_diagnostics



Data frame with one row for the full model and one row per candidate training partition. Required columns are ‘cv_strategy’, ‘repeat_id’, ‘effective_folds’, ‘fold_id’, ‘n_train_locations’, ‘n_train_samples’, ‘n_train_taxa’, and ‘n_train_mem_locations’. Supported strategies are ‘"full_model"’, ‘"spatially_stratified_group_kfold"’, and ‘"leave_one_location_out"’.





min_train_locations, min_train_samples, min_train_taxa



Positive integer thresholds required in the full model and every selected training partition.





min_mem_locations



Positive integer minimum number of locations required for MEM construction.





Details


The full model is checked first. Viable grouped candidates are preferred in ascending fold-count order, followed by leave-one-location-out. A viable full model without any viable holdout requires tier-pooled regularization.


Value


One-row tibble containing full-data counts, feasibility flags, selected ‘cv_strategy’, ‘effective_folds’, and ‘cv_feasibility_status’.


Examples

data_diagnostics <-
  tibble::tibble(
    cv_strategy = "full_model",
    repeat_id = 0L,
    effective_folds = NA_integer_,
    fold_id = 0L,
    n_train_locations = 7L,
    n_train_samples = 70L,
    n_train_taxa = 10L,
    n_train_mem_locations = 7L
  )
resolve_cross_validation_strategy(
  data_partition_diagnostics = data_diagnostics,
  min_train_locations = 5L,
  min_train_samples = 5L,
  min_train_taxa = 3L,

title: resolve_classification_to_finest_rank()
text:
resolve_classification_to_finest_rank


R Documentation




Resolve Classification to Finest Rank


Description


For each taxon in a wide-format taxonomic classification table, selects the value from the finest available rank (species > genus > family > order > class > phylum > kingdom). The result maps every ‘sel_name’ to a single ‘taxon_resolved’ value taken from the finest non-‘NA’ rank available.


Usage

resolve_classification_to_finest_rank(
  data_classification_table,
  vec_taxon_column_name = "taxon_resolved"
)


Arguments




data_classification_table



A wide-format data frame (e.g. output of ‘build_classification_table()’) containing a ‘sel_name’ column plus taxonomic rank columns: ‘kingdom’, ‘phylum’, ‘class’, ‘order’, ‘family’, ‘genus’, and ‘species’. All rank columns may contain ‘NA’ for unavailable ranks.





vec_taxon_column_name



A single non-empty character string giving the name of the output column that holds the resolved taxon name. Defaults to ‘"taxon_resolved"’.





Details


The function pivots the seven rank columns to long format, removes ‘NA’ rank values, assigns a numeric rank order (kingdom = 1, …, genus = 6, species = 7), and for each ‘sel_name’ retains the row with the highest rank order via ‘dplyr::slice_max()’. Ties are broken arbitrarily (‘with_ties = FALSE’). The rank order and the intermediate ‘rank’ column are dropped before returning, leaving only ‘sel_name’ and the column named by ‘vec_taxon_column_name’.


Value


A tibble with two columns: ‘sel_name’ (character) and the column named by ‘vec_taxon_column_name’ (character, default ‘"taxon_resolved"’). One row is returned per unique ‘sel_name’. The resolved column holds the taxon name at the finest available rank, or ‘NA’ if no rank column was non-‘NA’.


See Also


[build_classification_table()]

title: project_coords_to_metric()
text:
project_coords_to_metric


R Documentation




Project Geographic Coordinates to Metric (km)


Description


Converts WGS84 lon/lat coordinates to planar metric coordinates in kilometres using a user-specified equal-area projection. The original lon/lat columns are retained alongside the projected ‘coord_x_km’ and ‘coord_y_km’ columns.


Usage

project_coords_to_metric(data_coords = NULL, target_crs = 3035L)


Arguments




data_coords



A data frame with ‘dataset_name’ as row names and columns ‘coord_long’ and ‘coord_lat’ (decimal degrees, WGS84), as returned by ‘extract_dataset_coordinates()’.





target_crs



An integer EPSG code for the target projected coordinate reference system. Must be a metric (planar) equal-area CRS suitable for the geographic extent of the data. Defaults to ‘3035L’ (ETRS89 Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area, the standard for European analyses). For other regions, choose an appropriate equal-area projection, e.g.: * ‘6933L’ — EASE-Grid 2.0 (global) * ‘5070L’ — NAD83 Conus Albers (North America) * ‘102022L’ — Africa Albers Equal Area Conic (Africa)





Details


Using metric coordinates instead of degrees is necessary for distance-based spatial modelling (e.g., Moran eigenvectors) because degree distances are not uniform across latitudes. The ‘target_crs’ default of EPSG:3035 is the standard equal-area projection for European spatial analyses; change it for non-European study regions.


The function requires the sf package to perform coordinate transformation. Dataset names (row names) are preserved unchanged in the output.


Value


A data frame with the same row names and columns as ‘data_coords’, plus two additional columns:



‘coord_x_km’



Easting in kilometres (target CRS).



‘coord_y_km’



Northing in kilometres (target CRS).




See Also


[extract_dataset_coordinates()], [prepare_spatial_predictors_for_fit()]

title: prepare_classification_table_for_community_taxa()
text:
prepare_classification_table_for_community_taxa


R Documentation




Prepare a classification table for community taxa


Description


Re-keys a classification table so that ‘sel_name’ equals the classified taxon name at the specified ‘vec_taxonomic_resolution’, rather than the original raw pollen name. For each classified taxon name, one representative row is kept (preferring rows where the original ‘sel_name’ already matches the classified name). Rank columns finer than ‘vec_taxonomic_resolution’ are set to ‘NA_character_’ so that downstream ‘resolve_classification_to_finest_rank()’ returns the classified name as the canonical label rather than a species name.


Usage

prepare_classification_table_for_community_taxa(
  data_classification_table,
  data_community_classified,
  vec_taxonomic_resolution
)


Arguments




data_classification_table



A data frame mapping raw taxon names (‘sel_name’) to all taxonomic rank columns (‘kingdom’, ‘phylum’, ‘class’, ‘order’, ‘family’, ‘genus’, ‘species’). This is typically ‘data_combined_classification_table’ produced by ‘pipe_segment_community_prepare_paleo’.





data_community_classified



A data frame containing a ‘taxon’ column with the classified community taxon names (e.g. genus or family names). Used to determine which classified names are present in the community and should be retained in the output table.





vec_taxonomic_resolution



A single character string specifying the finest taxonomic rank to use for classification. Must be one of ‘"kingdom"’, ‘"phylum"’, ‘"class"’, ‘"order"’, ‘"family"’, ‘"genus"’, or ‘"species"’.





Details


Internally, ranks from ‘kingdom’ up to and including ‘vec_taxonomic_resolution’ are used to coalesce a ‘classified_name’ column via ‘dplyr::pick()’ and ‘purrr::reduce(dplyr::coalesce)’. The coalesce applies ranks from finest-to-coarsest (reversed) so that the most-specific available rank is used. After deduplication, ‘sel_name’ is replaced with ‘classified_name’ and finer rank columns are nulled out.


Value


A data frame with the same columns as ‘data_classification_table’ (‘sel_name’, ‘kingdom’, ‘phylum’, ‘class’, ‘order’, ‘family’, ‘genus’, ‘species’) where: - ‘sel_name’ is the classified taxon name (not the raw pollen name). - One row per classified taxon name (duplicate rows removed, direct-match rows preferred). - Rank columns finer than ‘vec_taxonomic_resolution’ are set to ‘NA_character_’. - Only classified names present in ‘data_community_classified’ are included.


See Also


[classify_taxonomic_resolution()], [resolve_classification_to_finest_rank()], [build_community_taxon_trait_table()]

title: plot_focal_trait_distribution()
text:
plot_focal_trait_distribution


R Documentation




Plot a Focal Taxon-Domain Trait Distribution


Description


Builds a ‘ggplot2’ strip + boxplot showing every raw trait value for one focal ‘taxon_name x trait_domain_name’ slice, with colour-coded Tukey fence flags and horizontal fence lines for both the standard (1.5x IQR) and extreme (3x IQR) thresholds.


Usage

plot_focal_trait_distribution(
  data_focal_trait_records,
  data_focal_trait_summary,
  focal_taxon,
  trait_domain,
  graphical_options,
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_focal_trait_records



A tibble of raw trait observations for one focal taxon-domain slice. Must contain columns ‘trait_value’ (numeric), ‘trait_name’ (character), and ‘trait_domain_name’ (character).





data_focal_trait_summary



A single-row tibble of focal-slice QC statistics, as produced by ‘write_trait_quality_control_report()’. Must contain numeric columns ‘mean’, ‘median’, ‘IQR’, and integer columns ‘n_suspected_outliers’ (integer) and ‘outlier_fraction’ (numeric).





focal_taxon



Character scalar. Name of the taxon being inspected. Used in the plot title.





trait_domain



Character scalar. Name of the trait domain being inspected. Used in the plot title.





graphical_options



Named list with elements ‘width’, ‘height’, ‘units’, ‘dpi’, and ‘bg’, as returned by ‘load_active_config_value("graphical")’. Passed to ‘ggview::canvas()’.





verbose



Logical. If ‘TRUE’ (default), the computed Tukey fence boundaries are printed to the console via ‘cli::cli_inform()’.





Details


The function computes Q1, Q3, and IQR from ‘data_focal_trait_records’ and derives four fence values: - inner lower / upper: Q1 - 1.5 * IQR and Q3 + 1.5 * IQR - outer lower / upper: Q1 - 3 * IQR and Q3 + 3 * IQR


Each observation is classified as ‘"within fence"’, ‘"mild outlier (1.5x IQR)"’, or ‘"extreme outlier (3x IQR)"’. When ‘data_focal_trait_records’ contains more than one distinct ‘trait_name’, observations are faceted by ‘trait_name’; otherwise the x-axis shows ‘trait_domain_name’.


Plot layer order follows project conventions: ‘ggplot()’ -> facets -> scales -> labels -> theme -> ‘ggview::canvas()’ -> geoms.


Value


A ‘ggplot2’ object. The plot is not printed; call ‘print()’ on the return value to display it.


See Also


[write_trait_quality_control_report()], [load_trait_corrections()], [validate_trait_corrections()], [correct_trait_records()]


Examples

## Not run:
data_focal_trait_records <-
  data_traits_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(
    taxon_name == "Anacyclus clavatus",
    trait_domain_name == "Leaf Area"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(trait_value)

data_focal_trait_summary <-
  data_qc_report |>
  dplyr::filter(
    taxon_name == "Anacyclus clavatus",
    trait_domain_name == "Leaf Area"
  )

graphical_options <-
  load_active_config_value("graphical")

p <-
  plot_focal_trait_distribution(
    data_focal_trait_records = data_focal_trait_records,
    data_focal_trait_summary = data_focal_trait_summary,
    focal_taxon = "Anacyclus clavatus",
    trait_domain = "Leaf Area",
    graphical_options = graphical_options
  )

base::print(p)

## End(Not run)

R Documentation




Load Trait Domain Names from VegVault


Description

Usage

load_trait_domain_names_from_vegvault(

load_taxa_classification


R Documentation




Load taxa classification


Description


Retrieves taxonomic classification for a vector of taxa using the taxospace package. Filters results to include only plant taxa. Results are cached on disk so that repeated calls for the same taxa avoid redundant HTTP requests.

A successful result is saved to cache; the empty dummy tibble returned on failure is never cached.

load_continental_trait_records_from_vegvault


R Documentation




Load Continental Trait Records from VegVault


Description


Loads raw trait data from VegVault for a single continental bounding box, removes incomplete records, and translates numeric taxon IDs to taxon names. Optionally prints progress messages.


Usage

load_continental_trait_records_from_vegvault(
  data_continental_unit,
  vec_trait_domain_names,
  path_vegvault = here::here("Data/Input/VegVault.sqlite"),
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_continental_unit



A single-row data frame (one continental unit from the spatial grid) with columns ‘scale_id’, ‘x_min’, ‘x_max’, ‘y_min’, and ‘y_max’.





vec_trait_domain_names



A non-empty character vector of trait domain names to extract (e.g. ‘c("Specific leaf area (SLA)", "Plant height vegetative")’).





path_vegvault



A single character string giving the path to the VegVault SQLite database (default: ‘here::here("Data/Input/VegVault.sqlite")’).





verbose



A single logical value. If ‘TRUE’ (default), progress messages are printed via ‘cli::cli_inform()’. Set to ‘FALSE’ to suppress all console output.

The function performs the following steps:



Validates all input arguments.
Derives the bounding-box limits and scale identifier from ‘data_continental_unit’.
Calls [load_trait_records_from_vegvault()] to retrieve raw records.
Calls [filter_complete_trait_records()] to drop incomplete rows.
Calls [resolve_trait_taxon_ids()] to replace numeric IDs with taxon names.
Returns the final tibble with taxon-name columns only.



Value


A tibble with columns ‘taxon_name’, ‘trait_domain_name’, ‘trait_name’, and ‘trait_value’, containing the cleaned and ID-resolved trait records for the supplied continental unit.

interpolate_paleo_community_with_age_uncertainty


R Documentation




Interpolate Paleo Community Data with Age Uncertainty


Description


Interpolates paleo community proportions to a regular time grid while incorporating per-sample age-model iterations for fossil pollen archives. Datasets without age-uncertainty records are interpolated using consensus ages. Fossil pollen archives are interpolated across their age-model iterations and reduced to the median proportion at each grid point.


Usage

interpolate_paleo_community_with_age_uncertainty(
  data_community,
  data_age_uncertainty,
  n_cores = 1L,
  max_expanded_rows = 4e+06,
  ...
)


Arguments




data_community



A data frame with columns ‘dataset_name’, ‘sample_name’, ‘taxon’, ‘age’, and ‘value’. Must already be in proportion form — see [prepare_community_proportions()].





data_age_uncertainty



A tibble produced by [extract_age_uncertainty_from_vegvault()], with columns ‘dataset_name’ (character), ‘sample_name’ (character), ‘iteration’ (integer), and ‘age_uncertainty’ (double). Rows for dataset names absent from ‘data_community’ are silently ignored.





n_cores



Number of workers to use for consensus-age interpolation. Fossil-core parallelism is handled by dynamic ‘targets’ branches in the paleo pipeline; use ‘1’ for branched fossil inputs.





max_expanded_rows



Maximum approximate number of expanded fossil observation rows processed in one interpolation batch (default: ‘4e6’). Lower values reduce peak memory use at the cost of more interpolation calls.





…



Additional arguments passed to [interpolate_grouped_time_series()], such as ‘time_step’, ‘age_min’, and ‘age_max’.





Details


Datasets present in ‘data_community’ that have no matching rows in ‘data_age_uncertainty’ are treated as gridpoints and interpolated using consensus ages. This ensures the function degrades gracefully when age uncertainty data are partially available.


The uncertainty-aware interpolation proceeds as follows for each fossil core: 1. The consensus ‘age’ column is dropped and replaced with ‘age_uncertainty’ (renamed to ‘age’) from ‘data_age_uncertainty’, expanding the data to one row per original observation per age-model iteration. 2. [interpolate_grouped_time_series()] is called grouped by ‘c("dataset_name", "taxon", "iteration")’. 3. The median ‘value’ across iterations is computed for each ‘(dataset_name, taxon, age)’ combination.


Fossil cores are joined and interpolated one dataset at a time, in bounded batches of age-model iterations, before each core is reduced. This bounds the expansion in continental runs, where joining all cores simultaneously can exceed available memory.


In the paleo pipelines, inputs are split into one dynamic target branch per dataset before this function is called. ‘targets’ therefore caches reduced core outputs and schedules parallel work externally.


Value


A data frame with columns ‘dataset_name’, ‘taxon’, ‘age’, and ‘value’ at regular time intervals. For fossil pollen archive datasets, ‘value’ is the median across age-model iterations.


See Also


[extract_age_uncertainty_from_vegvault()], [interpolate_grouped_time_series()]


Examples

data_community <- tibble::tibble(
  dataset_name = base::rep("core_a", 2L),
  sample_name = base::c("sample_1", "sample_2"),
  taxon = base::rep("Taxon", 2L),
  age = base::c(0, 100),
  value = base::c(0.25, 0.75)
)
data_age_uncertainty <- tibble::tibble(
  dataset_name = base::character(),
  sample_name = base::character(),
  iteration = base::integer(),
  age_uncertainty = base::numeric()
)
interpolate_paleo_community_with_age_uncertainty(
  data_community = data_community,
  data_age_uncertainty = data_age_uncertainty,
  age_min = 0,
  age_max = 100,
  time_step = 100
)

title: filter_constant_taxa()
text:
filter_constant_taxa


R Documentation




Filter Constant Taxa from Community Matrix


Description


Removes taxa that show no variation across all samples. A taxon is considered constant when its standard deviation is zero, meaning every sample has the same value. Constant taxa cannot contribute to any model likelihood and must be excluded before fitting. Filtering is applied regardless of the error family (binomial, Gaussian, Poisson, beta, etc.).


Usage

filter_constant_taxa(data_community_matrix = NULL)


Arguments




data_community_matrix



A numeric matrix with samples as rows and taxa as columns, as returned by ‘prepare_community_for_fit()’.





Details


Variation is assessed by computing ‘stats::sd()’ for each column via ‘purrr::map_dbl()’. A column is retained only when its standard deviation is strictly greater than zero. This family-agnostic approach replaces the previous binomial-only binarisation check and is now a tracked pipeline target.


Value


A numeric matrix of the same structure as the input, with all constant taxa (standard deviation equal to zero) removed. If no taxa are constant the input matrix is returned unchanged.


See Also


[prepare_community_for_fit()], [build_jsdm_fit_input()]

title: filter_community_to_plantae()
text:
filter_community_to_plantae


R Documentation




Filter Community to Plantae


Description


Removes taxa that do not belong to the kingdom Plantae from a community data frame, using a classification table to determine the kingdom assignment for each taxon.


Usage

filter_community_to_plantae(
  data_community,
  data_classification_table,
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_community



A data frame containing community data with at minimum a column named ‘taxon’.





data_classification_table



A data frame with columns ‘sel_name’ and ‘kingdom’, mapping taxon names to their kingdom classification.





verbose



Logical scalar. If ‘TRUE’, warn when non-Plantae or unclassified taxa are removed.





Details


Performs a left join between ‘data_community’ and ‘data_classification_table’ on ‘taxon == sel_name’ to retrieve the kingdom for each taxon. Any taxon where ‘kingdom’ is not exactly ‘"Plantae"’, including taxa with ‘kingdom = NA’, is treated as non-plant and removed. When any taxa are dropped, ‘cli::cli_warn()’ is issued reporting the count and the full vector of removed taxon names. Note: the upstream ‘load_taxa_classification()’ already filters to Plantae during the taxospace lookup, so in practice this function mainly catches taxa that are genuinely unclassifiable (i.e. not found in any classification source).


Value


A data frame identical in structure to ‘data_community’ but with all rows belonging to non-Plantae taxa removed. Taxa with ‘kingdom = NA’ (unclassifiable) are also removed.


See Also


[classify_taxonomic_resolution()], [filter_community_by_minimum_proportion()]

title: diagnose_jsdm_convergence()
text:
diagnose_jsdm_convergence


R Documentation




Diagnose sjSDM Model Convergence


Description


Assesses whether a fitted sjSDM model has converged by analysing the training loss history stored in the model object.


Usage

diagnose_jsdm_convergence(mod_jsdm = NULL)


Arguments




mod_jsdm



A fitted sjSDM model object. Must be of class ‘sjSDM’.





Details


The function uses the ‘history’ component of the fitted sjSDM model, which stores the per-epoch negative log-likelihood values produced during gradient descent.


sjSDM pre-allocates ‘history’ to the full epoch budget. When early stopping fires, the remaining trailing entries are zero. This function detects those trailing zeros, truncates the vector to only the epochs that were actually run, and sets ‘early_stopping_triggered = TRUE’.


Two diagnostic metrics are computed on the tail (final 10 epochs actually run):



Linear trend slope — A near-zero slope means the loss is no longer decreasing, indicating convergence. The recommended threshold is < 0.01.
Median difference — A robust comparison of the first versus last quarter of the tail using medians (insensitive to spikes). The recommended threshold is < 1.



Value


A list with six elements: - ‘linear_trend_slope’: Absolute slope of a linear trend fitted to the final 10 convergence. - ‘median_diff’: Absolute difference between the median of the first and last 25 convergence. - ‘convergence_plot’: A ggplot2 object showing the full loss history with a 20-epoch rolling median smoother. A dashed orange vertical line marks the last epoch run when early stopping was triggered. - ‘note’: A character string summarising the thresholds. - ‘epochs_run’: Integer. The number of epochs actually run before early stopping halted training (or the full budget when early stopping was not triggered). - ‘early_stopping_triggered’: Logical. ‘TRUE’ when the model stopped before exhausting its epoch budget (i.e. trailing zeros were detected in ‘mod_jsdm[["history"]]’).


See Also


[fit_jsdm_model()], [evaluate_jsdm()]

diagnose_cross_validation_partitions


R Documentation




Make Cross-Validation Partition Diagnostics


Description


Calculates full-model and fold-training counts from location assignments and aligned binary community responses for feasibility assessment.


Usage

diagnose_cross_validation_partitions(
  data_locations = NULL,
  data_assignments = NULL,
  data_community_matrix = NULL,
  cv_strategy = NULL,
  min_taxon_locations = 1L,
  min_taxon_samples = 1L,
  include_full_model = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_locations



Location table returned by [build_cross_validation_location_table()].





data_assignments



Assignment table returned by a cross-validation assignment helper. May be empty when ‘cv_strategy = "none"’ and only full-model diagnostics are required.





data_community_matrix



Numeric binary matrix with one row per original sample row and one column per taxon. Row positions must match location ‘row_indices’.





cv_strategy



Character scalar identifying the candidate strategy. Either ‘"spatially_stratified_group_kfold"’, ‘"leave_one_location_out"’, or ‘"none"’ for full-model-only diagnostics.





min_taxon_locations



Positive integer minimum number of training locations with a taxon presence.





min_taxon_samples



Positive integer minimum number of training samples with a taxon presence.





include_full_model



Logical scalar. If ‘TRUE’, prepend the full-model diagnostic row. Defaults to ‘TRUE’.





Details


Taxon viability is learned independently within each training partition. A retained binary taxon must meet both occurrence thresholds and contain at least one absence. MEM location counts equal the number of training locations; additional mode-specific MEM checks can raise the threshold in the feasibility assessor.


Value


Tibble matching [resolve_cross_validation_strategy()] input, with one optional full-model row and one row per repeat and fold.


Examples

  tibble::tibble(
    location_id = c("a", "b"),
    n_samples = c(1L, 1L),
    row_indices = list(1L, 2L)
  )
data_assignments <-
  build_leave_one_location_out_assignments(data_locations)
diagnose_cross_validation_partitions(
  data_locations = data_locations,
  data_assignments = data_assignments,
  data_community_matrix = matrix(c(0, 1), ncol = 1L),
  cv_strategy = "leave_one_location_out"
)

title: compute_spatiotemporal_mev()
text:
compute_spatiotemporal_mev


R Documentation




Compute Spatiotemporal Moran Eigenvector Maps


Description


Computes Moran Eigenvector Maps (MEMs) from a 3-D coordinate matrix ‘(x_km, y_km, age_kyr)’ built at the sample level (one row per site × time-slice). All three dimensions are z-scored before eigenvector computation so that spatial and temporal extents contribute equally to the Euclidean distance structure. Returns the first ‘n_mev’ eigenvectors as a data frame with row names in ’"dataset_name__age"’ format, ready for ‘scale_spatial_for_fit()’ and ‘build_jsdm_fit_input()’.


Usage

compute_spatiotemporal_mev(
  data_coords_projected = NULL,
  data_sample_ids = NULL,
  n_mev = 20L
)


Arguments




data_coords_projected



A data frame with ‘dataset_name’ as row names and columns ‘coord_x_km’ and ‘coord_y_km’, as returned by ‘project_coords_to_metric()’. One row per unique site/core.





data_sample_ids



A data frame with columns ‘dataset_name’ and ‘age’ giving the valid (site × time-slice) pairs to model, as returned by ‘align_sample_ids()’.





n_mev



A positive integer giving the number of eigenvectors to return. If it exceeds the number of positive Moran eigenvectors produced by ‘sjSDM::generateSpatialEV()’ for the 3-D coordinate matrix, it is automatically clamped down to that count and a ‘cli::cli_warn()’ message is emitted. Default is ‘20L’.





Details


Unlike ‘compute_spatial_mev()’, which operates on unique site coordinates and must be expanded to sample level via ‘prepare_spatial_predictors_for_fit()’, this function builds the eigenvectors directly on the sample-level 3-D coordinate matrix. This means each observation (site × age) gets a unique row in the MEV matrix, and within-core temporal autocorrelation is captured alongside between-site spatial autocorrelation.


The 3-D coordinate matrix is constructed as follows: 1. Join ‘data_coords_projected’ (x_km, y_km) onto ‘data_sample_ids’ to get one row per sample. 2. Convert age (years BP) to kiloyears: ‘age_kyr = age / 1000’. 3. Z-score each dimension independently so that the spatial and temporal extents are on the same scale before Euclidean distances are computed.


The z-scoring step is critical: if age is left in kiloyears and coordinates in km, the time axis will dominate or be negligible depending on the data range, producing eigenvectors that are either purely temporal or purely spatial.


Because the eigenvectors are computed at the sample level, no further expansion step is required. Pass the returned data frame directly to ‘scale_spatial_for_fit()’.


Value


A data frame with row names ’"<dataset_name>__<age>"’ and ‘n_mev’ columns named ‘mev_1’, ‘mev_2’, …, ‘mev_n_mev’. The row order follows ‘data_sample_ids’ sorted by ‘dataset_name’ then ‘age’, matching the ordering produced by ‘prepare_abiotic_for_fit()’ and ‘prepare_community_for_fit()’.


See Also


[compute_spatial_mev()], [project_coords_to_metric()], [align_sample_ids()], [scale_spatial_for_fit()], [build_jsdm_fit_input()]

Character vector of network-level indices to compute, passed directly to the ‘index’ argument of ‘bipartite::networklevel()’. Default: ‘c("connectance", "nestedness", "modularity")’.





Details


The function treats the community matrix as a lower-level (samples) × upper-level (taxa) bipartite network. Only the binary incidence (presence/absence) is used: all values > 0 are set to 1 before passing to ‘bipartite::networklevel()’.


If the binarized matrix has no positive entries (i.e. no species observed in any sample), an error is raised.


Value


A ‘tibble’ with two columns:



‘metric’



Character. Name of the network metric.



‘value’



Numeric. Computed value of the metric.

title: compute_jsdm_se()
text:
compute_jsdm_se


R Documentation




Compute Standard Errors for a Fitted sjSDM Model


Description


Post-hoc calculation of standard errors for a fitted sjSDM model using ‘sjSDM::getSe()’. This is intentionally separated from ‘fit_jsdm_model()’ so that the GPU-based model fitting step and the CPU-based SE computation step can be run independently, allowing the SE step to exploit all available CPU cores without being constrained by the GPU device setting.


Usage

compute_jsdm_se(
  mod_jsdm = NULL,
  parallel = 0L,
  step_size = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)


Arguments




mod_jsdm



An object of class ‘sjSDM’ returned by ‘fit_jsdm_model()’ or ‘sjSDM::sjSDM()’. Must not be ‘NULL’.





parallel



Number of CPU cores to use for the data loader during SE computation. Passed to the ‘parallel’ argument of ‘sjSDM::getSe()’. Default is ‘0L’ (no parallelisation). Use the ‘n_cores’ value from ‘config.model_fitting’ in the project configuration to exploit all available cores.





step_size



Batch size for stochastic gradient descent used during SE computation. Passed to ‘sjSDM::getSe()’. Default is ‘NULL’, which lets sjSDM choose automatically.





verbose



Logical scalar. If ‘FALSE’ (default), all console output from ‘sjSDM::getSe()’ — including Python/reticulate stdout — is suppressed. Set to ‘TRUE’ to see progress messages, which is recommended when running inside a pipeline target to monitor long-running SE computation.





Details


‘sjSDM::getSe()’ uses CPU for SE computation regardless of the device used for model fitting. Separating SE computation into its own pipeline target therefore allows the caller to pass the full number of available CPU cores via ‘parallel’ without conflict with the GPU device setting used during fitting.


When ‘verbose = FALSE’, output is captured with ‘reticulate::py_capture_output()’ (Python stdout) and ‘utils::capture.output()’ (R stdout) so the console remains clean. When ‘verbose = TRUE’, both output streams are printed for monitoring progress.


If SE computation fails, the function raises an error with an informative message.


Value


The input ‘mod_jsdm’ object with its ‘se’ field populated with the computed standard errors.


See Also


‘sjSDM::getSe’, ‘fit_jsdm_model’

title: compute_cross_validation_grid_calibration()
text:
compute_cross_validation_grid_calibration


R Documentation




Calibrate Cross-Validation Grid Size


Description


Compares candidate spatial-grid sizes using occupied-cell density and fold balance, then marks the finest eligible candidate.


Usage

compute_cross_validation_grid_calibration(
  data_locations = NULL,
  candidate_grid_cell_sizes_km = NULL,
  n_folds = 5L,
  n_repeats = 1L,
  occupancy_criterion = "median",
  target_locations_per_cell = NULL,
  lower_quantile_probability = 0.25,
  max_fold_location_difference = 1L,
  max_fold_sample_difference = Inf,
  seed = 900723L
)


Arguments




data_locations



Location table returned by [build_cross_validation_location_table()].





candidate_grid_cell_sizes_km



Numeric vector of unique positive candidate grid-cell widths in kilometres.





n_folds



Single integer greater than one and no greater than the location count.





n_repeats



Single positive integer used to evaluate deterministic origin shifts.





occupancy_criterion



Character scalar: ‘"minimum"’, ‘"lower_quantile"’, or ‘"median"’.





target_locations_per_cell



Positive numeric occupancy target. Defaults to ‘n_folds’ when ‘NULL’.





lower_quantile_probability



Probability used by ‘"lower_quantile"’, between zero and ‘0.5’. Defaults to ‘0.25’.





max_fold_location_difference



Maximum allowed difference between the largest and smallest fold location counts within any repeat. Defaults to ‘1L’.





max_fold_sample_difference



Maximum allowed difference between fold sample counts within any repeat. Defaults to ‘Inf’ so it is diagnostic until calibrated explicitly.





seed



Single non-negative integer assignment seed. Defaults to ‘900723L’.





Details


Candidate assignments use [build_spatial_cross_validation_assignments()]. Eligibility requires the configured occupancy statistic and both balance thresholds. Among eligible candidates, the smallest cell size is selected.


Value


Tibble with one row per candidate grid size, occupancy and balance diagnostics, eligibility, selection status, and a single ‘selected’ flag when at least one candidate is eligible.


Examples

data_locations <-
  tibble::tibble(
    location_id = letters[1:6],
    coord_x_km = c(0, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12),
    coord_y_km = rep(0, 6),
    n_samples = rep(1L, 6),
    row_indices = as.list(seq_len(6L))
  )
compute_cross_validation_grid_calibration(
  data_locations = data_locations,
  candidate_grid_cell_sizes_km = c(1, 10),
  n_folds = 3L
)

title: classify_to_functional_type()
text:
classify_to_functional_type


R Documentation




Classify Community Data to Functional Types


Description


Classifies taxa in a long-format community data frame to functional-type (FT) labels using a pre-computed FT classification table. Aggregates pollen proportions by all non-‘taxon’/‘value’ identifier columns plus functional type. Produces the same output column structure as ‘classify_taxonomic_resolution()’ so it can be used as a drop-in replacement downstream.


Usage

classify_to_functional_type(
  data_source,
  data_functional_type_classification,
  verbose = TRUE
)


Arguments




data_source



A data frame containing community data with columns ‘taxon’, ‘dataset_name’, ‘age’, and ‘value’. Other identifier columns such as ‘sample_name’ are preserved.





data_functional_type_classification



A data frame mapping taxa to functional types. Must contain columns ‘taxon_name’ (character) and ‘functional_type’ (integer). Typically produced by ‘assign_functional_type_clusters()’ and loaded via ‘load_latest_functional_type_classification()’.





verbose



Logical. Reserved for informational progress messages. The warning emitted when unmatched taxa are dropped is always shown because it reports data loss.





Details


Steps performed:




Validate arguments.




Left-join ‘data_source’ to ‘data_functional_type_classification’ on their taxon names.




Drop unmatched taxa (NA functional type) with a warning.




Create ‘taxon’ labels ‘"FT_functional_type"’.




Aggregate ‘value’ by original identifier columns and ‘taxon’.




Full-join back to an identifier/taxon cross-reference to preserve true negatives.




Value


A data frame with the same column names as ‘data_source’. The ‘taxon’ column is replaced by functional-type labels of the form ‘"FT_1"’, ‘"FT_2"’, etc. ‘value’ is aggregated (summed) by all original identifier columns and ‘taxon’. All identifier combinations present after FT classification are preserved (true negatives kept via a cross-reference join). Taxa not found in ‘data_functional_type_classification’ are dropped with a ‘cli::cli_warn()’ message.


See Also


[classify_taxonomic_resolution()], [load_latest_functional_type_classification()], [assign_functional_type_clusters()]

build_repeated_diagnostic_fold_indices


R Documentation




Make Repeated Cross-Validation Indices


Description


Creates reproducible repeated K-fold test-index lists for project-owned decomposition diagnostics with [run_decomposition_diagnostic_folds()].


Usage

build_repeated_diagnostic_fold_indices(
  n_samples,
  n_folds = 2L,
  n_repeats = 1L,
  seed = 900723L
)


Arguments




n_samples



Single integer. Number of samples to split into folds.





n_folds



Single integer. Number of folds per repeat. Default is ‘2L’.





n_repeats



Single integer. Number of repeated fold partitions. Default is ‘1L’.





seed



Single integer. Random seed used for reproducible fold assignment.





Value


A named list with one element per repeat. Each repeat is a named list of integer test indices, one element per fold.


Examples

build_repeated_diagnostic_fold_indices(
  n_samples = 8L,
  n_folds = 2L,
  n_repeats = 2L,
  seed = 900723L
)

title: build_leave_one_location_out_assignments()
text:
build_leave_one_location_out_assignments


R Documentation




Make Leave-One-Location-Out Assignments


Description


Assigns each complete sampling location to its own held-out fold using the shared cross-validation assignment schema.


Usage

build_leave_one_location_out_assignments(data_locations = NULL, repeat_id = 1L)


Arguments




data_locations



Location table returned by [build_cross_validation_location_table()] with ‘location_id’, ‘n_samples’, and ‘row_indices’ columns.





repeat_id



Single positive integer identifying the assignment repeat. Defaults to ‘1L’.





Value


Tibble with ‘repeat_id’, ‘fold_id’, ‘location_id’, ‘grid_cell_id’, ‘n_samples’, and ‘row_indices’. ‘grid_cell_id’ is ‘NA’ because spatial-grid stratification is not applicable to leave-one-location-out assignment.


Examples

data_locations <-
  tibble::tibble(
    location_id = c("core_a", "core_b"),
    n_samples = c(2L, 1L),
    row_indices = list(c(1L, 2L), 3L)
  )
build_leave_one_location_out_assignments(data_locations)
